item.title: Java Programming Study Guide - OOPS
item.description:
Java Programming Study Guide - OOPS

Intermediate

1. Demonstrate Upcasting in a main method.

Solution:

class Parent { void show() { System.out.println("Parent"); } }
class Child extends Parent { void show() { System.out.println("Child"); } }

public class Main {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        Parent p = new Child(); // Upcasting
        p.show();
    }
}

2. Demonstrate the use of abstract class and private fields with getters.

Solution:

abstract class Vehicle {
    private String name;
    public Vehicle(String name) { this.name = name; }
    public String getName() { return name; }
    abstract void start();
}

Advanced

3. Write a program that demonstrates the four pillars of OOPS (Abstraction, Encapsulation, Inheritance, and Polymorphism) using an Animal superclass and a Dog subclass.

Solution:

}

public class Main {
    public static void main(String[] args) {

abstract class Employee {
    private String name; // Encapsulation

    public Employee(String name) { this.name = name; }

    public String getName() { return name; } // Getter

    abstract void work(); // Abstraction
}

class Developer extends Employee {
    public Developer(String name) { super(name); }

}

    // 2. Encapsulation
    private String name;

    public Animal(String name) { this.name = name; }

    public String getName() { return name; }

    public abstract void makeSound();
}

// 3. Inheritance
class Dog extends Animal {
    public Dog(String name) { super(name); }

    // 4. Polymorphism (Overriding)
    @Override
    public void makeSound() {
        System.out.println(getName() + " says: Woof!");
    }
}

public class OOPSDemo {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        Animal myDog = new Dog("Buddy"); // Upcasting (Polymorphism)
        myDog.makeSound(); 
    }
}
